name: Image
first: A view that shows a picture or a symbol, at the picture's own size unless it is made resizable.

dependsOn.why: An image is a view that SwiftUI provides.
An image is made to fit its space with modifiers.
Whether an image takes the size it is proposed, or keeps its own, is the image's choice in the steps of layout.

what.is: An `Image` is a view that shows a picture, from the app's assets or from a file, or one of Apple's symbols. Unless it is made resizable, it keeps the picture's own size, whatever size it is proposed.
what.afterExample: Each renderer proposes 300 by 200 points. The plain star keeps its own size, 17 by 16. With `resizable()` it takes the whole proposal, 300 by 200, and stretches. With `scaledToFit()` as well, it grows as far as it can while it keeps its shape: 215 by 200.
what.problem: Pictures come in their own sizes, and screens do not. An image shows a picture at its own size, and two modifiers let it grow or shrink to the space it is given, without stretching it out of shape.
what.how: In the steps of layout, a plain `Image` chooses the picture's own size. The modifier `resizable()` makes it choose the size it is proposed. `scaledToFit()` then keeps the picture's shape, and chooses the largest size of that shape that fits the proposal.

when.text: Use `resizable()` with `scaledToFit()` for a picture that should fill as much of its space as it can, and still keep its shape.
Don't use `resizable()` alone on a picture that has a shape to keep: it stretches the picture to the proposal, as the star at 300 by 200.
